metadata.chapter_subtitle: Measuring Earth from a distance with light, heat, sound, and microwave energy

inventory.summary: The series had supporting remote-sensing material, but it lacked a direct beginner-facing entry chapter that explains what remote sensing is, how sensors differ from one another, and why modelling starts with measurement choices.
issues: Readers could meet remote-sensing applications before getting a plain-language definition of the field itself.
The core book needed a conceptual bridge from observation to model input.
Passive and active sensing needed to be distinguished before specialist chapters introduced their own methods.

rewrite.summary: Added a new foundations chapter that introduces remote sensing through the idea of measuring Earth from a distance, compares common sensor families, and keeps the modelling frame visible from the start.
editor_notes: Kept the language introductory and concrete so the chapter works for first-time readers.
Used familiar examples such as cameras, thermal sensors, radar, and sonar before shifting into formal terminology.
Made the connection between sensed signals and computational models explicit.

qa_review.summary: The chapter establishes remote sensing cleanly at the right level for the core-book volume and gives readers the intuition they need before later spectral and orbital chapters become more technical.

repair.summary: The missing introduction was repaired by adding a new chapter and placing it before the more technical remote-sensing foundations.
actions_taken: Added a new introductory remote-sensing chapter to the foundations sequence.
Linked the chapter into the core-book configuration and part index.
Positioned the chapter as the conceptual start of a broader remote-sensing ladder.

design_review.summary: The chapter uses comparison visuals and sensor-family explainers to help readers see the structure of the topic before the terminology accumulates.
improvements_made: Added a learner-facing Before You Start block to surface prerequisites.
Used a sensor comparison visual to show how different observation systems measure different parts of the world.
Explained how each sensor family feeds later models rather than leaving the examples descriptive only.
